summary:
The Odyssey: No Limits is an interactive 3D space mission design and exploration game that combines creativity, engineering and scientific learning.

Players can explore a growing selection of space missions, each presenting unique objectives and challenges that require them to design and build their own spacecraft, orbiters and rovers.

These challenges involve exploring Mars, collecting and transmitting scientific data, managing resources, constructing outposts and sustaining human life on another planet. Players must make important engineering decisions, balancing factors such as spacecraft mass, electrical power, mission budgets and available resources.

Currently, the game features one playable mission, Project Red Horizon, which is still incomplete. This mission focuses on Mars exploration and the establishment of a human outpost.

By incorporating real NASA data, established physics principles and simplified engineering simulations, our game aims to make space exploration more educational, engaging and accessible, encouraging players to think creatively and solve real-world engineering challenges.
details:
The Odyssey: No Limits

an interactive 3D space mission design and exploration game developed to make aerospace engineering, planetary science, and space exploration more accessible and engaging.

Our goal is to allow players to experience the challenges faced by real mission planners and engineers. Rather than simply exploring space, players must design their own spacecraft, make engineering decisions, manage limited resources, and overcome mission challenges.

The game is designed as an expandable platform featuring different space missions. Currently, its first playable mission is PROJECT RED HORIZON, focused on exploring Mars and establishing a sustainable human outpost.

How the game works?
This is only for mission PROJECT RED HORIZON.

Players begin at Mission Control, where they receive a briefing outlining their objectives.

The mission progresses through several interconnected stages:

1. Spacecraft Design: Players assemble orbiters and rovers using modular components while balancing engineering constraints such as mass, electrical power, equipment compatibility, and mission budgets

2. Mars Exploration: Players deploy their rover onto the Martian surface, navigate challenging terrain, investigate scientific checkpoints, and collect information about the surrounding environment.

3. Site Assessment: Players examine the Martian landscape and identify a suitable location for a future human outpost, considering terrain accessibility and environmental conditions.

4. Cargo and Infrastructure: Players design cargo spacecraft, select essential supplies and equipment, and prepare the infrastructure needed to support human exploration.

5. Human Outpost Operations: Players manage a Mars outpost through a three-sol campaign, carrying out tasks involving power generation, water management, greenhouse operations, communications, and exploration.

Players will receive feedback on their decisions and mission performance, encouraging experimentation and improvement.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Scientific Accuracy and Engineering

A major objective of our project is to connect enjoyable gameplay with real scientific principles.

Our engineering systems incorporate simplified mathematical models involving orbital mechanics, gravity, spacecraft mass, electrical power, and resource management.

We referenced publicly available NASA scientific resources, including information about Mars, its orbital environment, planetary characteristics, exploration technologies, and the challenges of sustaining human life beyond Earth.

Players are encouraged to understand engineering trade-offs: increasing equipment capacity may also increase mass, power consumption, and cost.

Although some systems are simplified for educational accessibility and gameplay, the project aims to demonstrate the principles behind real space mission planning rather than presenting purely fictional spacecraft mechanics.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Tools and Development

The game was developed using Godot 4, with GDScript as its primary programming language and Visual Studio Code as a development environment.

We used ChatGPT and OpenAI Codex to assist with programming, debugging, research, simulation development, and testing.

Our development process also involved iterative gameplay testing, numerical validation of selected engineering calculations, and continuous improvements to the game's visual presentation and user experience. <-------this wording is ai generated HAH.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Creativity and Design

Our approach combines spacecraft engineering, planetary exploration, and outpost management within a single connected mission.

We chose a stylized 3D visual direction to make complex scientific concepts more approachable while maintaining immersive environments, interactive spacecraft construction, and cinematic mission sequences.

Throughout development, I prioritized scientific credibility, educational value, visual clarity, user accessibility, and engaging gameplay.

I personally drew and sketched all the designs, taking inspiration from REAL NASA mission and data. Later on it was refurbished as a 3D animated cartoonish style.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Intended Impact and Future Potential

THE ODYSSEY aims to inspire students and aspiring engineers to explore STEM fields through hands-on learning.

By allowing players to experiment with spacecraft designs and experience the consequences of engineering decisions, the game encourages critical thinking, creativity, problem-solving, and scientific curiosity.
This is heavily due to the fact that i admire and aspire to become an engineer one day.

With further development, we envision expanding the game to include lunar missions, asteroid exploration, additional planetary destinations, more advanced physics simulations, open world and multiplayer access, and a mission creator for students and educators.
